headline: Reviewed First Student transportation contract follow-up and student activity fund review; no votes were taken.
summary: The subcommittee reviewed the First Student transportation contract follow-up report and the student activity funds review. Most of the 14 recommendations from the 2024 audit were implemented, and two remain in process. No formal votes were taken.

Public Portion 
 1. Presentation and discussion of the First Student Transportation Services Contract 
Follow up Review. 
 2. Presentation and discussion of the School Year 2025 Student Activities Agreed Upon 
Procedures Report. 
 
Minutes: 
On September 25, 2026, the Audit Committee, chaired by Councilor Justin Hurst, met virtually 
at 12:04 p.m. to review the Student Transportation Services Follow-Up Report and Student 
Activity Funds Review. Councilors Kateri Walsh and Victor Davila participated, along with 
School Committee Member Rosa Valentin, Superintendent Dr. Sonia Dinnall, Auditor Yong No, 
Pat Roach, and other City and School Department representatives. The transportation follow-up 
found that most of the 14 recommendations from the 2024 audit had been implemented, 
including improvements to required insurance and performance bond documentation, EpiPen 
training and drug and alcohol testing records, bus identification, operational reporting, billing 
procedures, written procedures, and customer service. First Student reported approximately 95 
percent on-time performance for large and minibuses during the 2024-2025 school year. 
 
Two transportation recommendations remained in process. Approximately 22 vehicles had 
unresolved registration and excise tax issues, and some buses exceeded contractual age or 
mileage limits. First Student is addressing the registration issues and has a fleet replacement 
plan, while the School Department is implementing additional monitoring procedures. The 
Auditor agreed to determine the potential financial impact of the outstanding excise taxes. The 
committee also reviewed 179 student activity accounts totaling approximately $373,000. The 
overall policies and accounting framework were found generally adequate, with some issues 
identified involving cash deposits, supporting documentation, reconciliation, purchasing 
procedures, refunds, and sales tax charges. The School Department agreed to continue 
monitoring and training staff on required procedures.
The committee briefly discussed cybersecurity as a potential future Audit Committee topic. 
Auditor No reported that regular cybersecurity reviews are conducted and that a future meeting 
would be scheduled regarding a recent City review, with sensitive findings generally addressed 
in executive session when appropriate. No formal votes were taken. The Student Transportation 
Services Follow-Up Report and Student Activity Funds Review were the documents presented 
and reviewed. The meeting adjourned at approximately 12:36 p.m.
